claims.text: The reference potential should be replaced with a machine-learning interatomic potential.
The machine-learning potential should be trained explicitly on diverse ab initio configurations of the multicomponent liquid.
Machine-learning potentials can reproduce DFT energies and forces accurately in multicomponent refractory HEAs.
Training on diverse liquid configurations will improve representation of local atomic environments, short-range correlations, and fluctuations in the ab initio liquid.
The trained machine-learning potential will reproduce the liquid-state energy landscape more faithfully than a conventional EAM reference.
A more faithful liquid energy landscape will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be reduced by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The resulting free-energy estimates will fall within a preset tolerance of directly converged ab initio calculations.
TOR-TILD's traditional EAM references inadequately represent the multitude of liquid configurations in multicomponent HEAs.
The representational limitations of EAM references cause significant phase-space-overlap deficiencies and integration-path mismatches.
Classical EAM/Lennard-Jones parameters have produced properties in quantitative agreement with first-principles calculations and experiments for quinary Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni.
The proposed intervention applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEAs containing four or more elements.
The proposed intervention applies over approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm.
The proposed intervention applies to both liquid and solid phases near melting.
The hypothesis may fail for alloys with extreme atomic-size discrepancies or at temperatures far from melting.
Elemental and binary calculations provide evidence that machine-learning potentials substantially improve reference quality.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality and breadth of the ab initio training set.
Failure to obtain an approximately 50% mismatch reduction or a statistically significant overlap improvement relative to EAM would falsify the hypothesis.
